stumbles.quote: `--bits` sets the quantization width used for the search.
stumbles.why: The text never says how this relates to the index. It doesn't say whether the index must have been built with a matching bit width, or what quantization the index uses. Nothing here explains how to build an index.

stumbles.quote: If the index was built with `--keep-float`
stumbles.why: `--keep-float` is a build option that this section never introduces, and the build command is not shown. A reader can't tell how to check or set it.

stumbles.quote: `query` is the line number of the query in `QUERY_FILE`.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say whether numbering starts at 0 or 1. The example shows `"query": 1`, which doesn't settle it.

stumbles.quote: `ids` and `scores` hold the matched vectors and their scores.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say what the ids refer to (the position in the build input or something else). It also doesn't say whether a higher score is better, or whether scores are similarity or distance.

stumbles.quote: every search rescores its top 100 candidates
stumbles.why: It's unclear whether 100 is fixed or configurable. It's also unclear what happens when `-k` is greater than 100. The text doesn't say whether `--bits` affects the candidate stage only.
The test set is not explained or linked. The recall figures also don't say whether they were measured with or without rescoring, so they are hard to interpret.

point: `remex search INDEX QUERY_FILE` reads comma-separated query vectors and writes JSON Lines of top-k ids and scores. `--bits` trades recall for speed, and rescoring happens only if the index was built with `--keep-float`.
